clauses.clause: Put a +1/+1 counter on target creature you control,
clauses.evidence: target slot (cast): 1..1 of [you_bear, you_giant], your creatures only (no opp_* creature offered); [cast targets=['you_bear']]: first event 'you_bear gets 1 PLUS_1_PLUS_1 counter(s)'; mana G-1 W-2 = {2}{G}; the instant goes to the graveyard. Tree identical to parse (template B5b-double-counters-target).

clauses.clause: then double the number of +1/+1 counters on that creature.
clauses.evidence: [cast targets=['you_bear']]: second PUT_COUNTER adds 1 (0 -> 1 -> 2), you_bear 2/2 -> 4/4; same on you_giant 4/4 -> 6/6. The trace starts from 0 counters, so a fixed +1 would look the same: pack invigorating_surge_doubles_existing.json (second cast 2 -> 3 -> 6, 8/8) PASS; pack invigorating_surge_x_conclave_mentor.json (CR 701.10e: doubling gives counters, so Mentor's +1 applies twice: 5 counters) PASS.
clauses.issue: engine note, not a fault in M21: QProp(referent='target', COUNTER_COUNT) sums every counter kind on the creature (MTG_bot/core/executor/quantity.py:504-505), not only +1/+1. Exact in M21, where creatures only ever carry +1/+1 counters; with -1/-1 or other counters on the creature (other sets) the doubling would be stronger than printed.
